scenes.line1: Why do services fail to start?
scenes.say: Ever wondered why a service won't start in Linux? It's almost always a systemd problem.

scenes.label: Unit
scenes.sub: systemd reads unit files to launch and manage services.
scenes.say: Systemd launches and supervises services using unit files. Your custom units go in slash etc slash systemd slash system.

scenes.code:
[Unit]
Description=My App
After=network.target

[Service]
User=app
ExecStart=/opt/myapp/run.sh
Restart=on-failure

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
scenes.say: Here's a sample unit file. It describes when to start, which user to run as, and how to restart.

scenes.title: Manage your service
scenes.say: Reload systemd, enable and start your service, check status, and view logs in real time.

scenes.question: What does 'enable --now' do?
scenes.wrong: Just enables the service on boot.
scenes.right: It enables the service on boot and starts it immediately.
scenes.say: Interview trap: 'Enable dash dash now' both enables your service at boot and starts it right away.
